title: A role resolves a base merge whose conflicts touch both test and product files
why: No role may resolve a base merge whose conflicts touch both test and product files, so the orchestrator resolved one by hand on PR #1619 (coordinator, 17:05 CST Nov 7). That breaks roles-orchestrator-never-builds.
note: Done check: a mixed-conflict merge goes to a named role, with no orchestrator edit. Built as #1683, with runner 8: round 3 PASS, net value positive (coordinator 18:44 CST). Done when #1683 merges. Follow-up: merge-commit-role-scope. 18:54 CST: the Fix-line commits pushed onto #1683's reviewed head are reverted; the lines move to the stacked PR (merge-commit-role-scope). Guard: step reviewed-head-push-ask. Incident (20:05 CST, lane notes-fix-large-3, proposed step test-conflict-merge-route): merging stacked #1687 into #1722 left a conflict in hooks/test_guard.py. The builder was refused, no other role could finish the merge on main's rules, and the orchestrator removed the three marker lines itself. #1683's test-author carve-out (decision builders-cannot-edit-tests: mid-merge, a test-author writes a still-unmerged file in its own worktree) is that route, so no new step was filed. Follow-up (coordinator 21:10 CST): once #1675 lands, #1683's branch drops debt builder-edits-mutation-config, which #1675 retires. Added 21:11 CST. New sighting (lane lint-uses-pinned-tools, coordinator 01:03 CST Nov 8): a main merge that conflicted in a test file only had no role to resolve it, so the lane resolved it by hand (#1461 or #1481). Folded here as suggested slug merge-conflict-in-test-file: check that this step's route also covers a conflict in test files only (a test-author resolves it); if it does not, widen it in a follow-up, not mid-review.
